questions.subject: science
questions.question: On which law/principle is a lactometer based?
questions.explanation: A lactometer floats in liquid. So it works on Archimedes' principle.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is the condition for a hydrogen balloon to fly upward in air?
options: Weight of balloon = weight of air displaced
Weight of balloon > weight of air displaced
Weight of balloon = volume of air displaced
Weight of balloon < weight of air displaced
questions.explanation: A hydrogen balloon rises when upthrust is greater than its weight. This happens when its weight is less than displaced air.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: In a hydraulic machine, the larger piston has twice the area of the smaller piston. Which weights keep it balanced?
questions.explanation: In a hydraulic machine, pressure is the same in both pistons. Double area needs double force to balance.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: An object is weighed in air, water and glycerin as W1, W2 and W3 respectively. What is the increasing order of apparent weight?
questions.explanation: Glycerin is denser than water, so it gives more upthrust. More upthrust means less apparent weight.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: When a ship enters a river from a sea, it sinks more than before. What is the reason?
options: Seawater temperature is more than river water
Seawater temperature is less than river water
Seawater density is more than river water
Seawater density is less than river water
questions.explanation: Sea water is denser than river water. River water gives less upthrust, so the ship sinks more.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which statement is correct for a hand pushing a ball into water?
options: Upthrust increases until the ball completely sinks
Equal pressure acts on all parts of the ball
The more the ball is pushed, the less upthrust it experiences
questions.explanation: When more part of the ball enters water, more water is displaced. So upthrust increases until it fully sinks.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: If equal upthrust acts on three cubical balls made of different materials in water, which quantity is equal for them?
questions.explanation: In the same liquid, equal upthrust means equal displaced volume. So the volume is equal.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is the upthrust when the cork shown in the textbook figure is placed in liquid?
questions.explanation: Upthrust is found by loss of weight in liquid. It equals weight in air minus apparent weight.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is pressure?
questions.explanation: Pressure means force on unit area. So pressure = force / area.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is the SI unit of pressure?
questions.explanation: Pascal is the SI unit of pressure. It is written as Pa.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which formula gives pressure?
questions.explanation: Pressure is force per unit area. So the formula is P = F/A.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Why does a sharp knife cut better than a blunt knife?
options: It produces more pressure due to smaller area
questions.explanation: A sharp knife has a smaller edge area. Same force on small area gives more pressure.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What happens to pressure when the same force acts on a larger area?
questions.explanation: Pressure decreases when area increases. This is because pressure = force / area.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What does Pascal's law state?
options: Heat flows from cold to hot body only
Pressure applied to an enclosed liquid is transmitted equally in all directions
Light always travels in curved lines
questions.explanation: Pascal's law says pressure in enclosed liquid spreads equally. It acts in all directions.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which device uses Pascal's law?
questions.explanation: A hydraulic brake uses liquid pressure. So it works on Pascal's law.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is a hydraulic machine?
options: A machine that transmits pressure through liquid to multiply force
A tool for measuring light speed
A machine that needs no liquid
questions.explanation: A hydraulic machine uses liquid to transmit pressure. This helps multiply force.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Why is a special oil used in hydraulic brakes?
options: It transmits pressure effectively and does not compress easily
questions.explanation: Hydraulic oil does not compress easily. So it transmits pressure properly.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is upthrust?
options: Upward force exerted by a fluid on an immersed object
Downward force due to weight only
questions.explanation: Upthrust is the upward force of fluid. It acts on an object placed in fluid.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What causes upthrust in a liquid?
options: Pressure is equal at every depth only
Pressure is greater at lower depth than upper depth
questions.explanation: Liquid pressure is greater at greater depth. This pressure difference produces upthrust.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which principle states that upthrust equals the weight of liquid displaced?
questions.explanation: Archimedes' principle says upthrust equals weight of displaced liquid. It explains floating and sinking.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Why do we feel lighter while floating in water?
options: Water provides upthrust that reduces apparent weight
The body loses all weight permanently
questions.explanation: Water gives upward force on the body. This reduces apparent weight, so we feel lighter.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Why does a stone feel heavier when lifted out of water?
options: Air gives more upthrust than water
Upthrust disappears or decreases outside water
questions.explanation: Outside water, the support from upthrust becomes very small. So the stone feels heavier.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Why is floating easier in the Dead Sea than in a swimming pool?
options: Dead Sea water has higher density and gives more upthrust
Dead Sea water has no gravity
Dead Sea water has no pressure
questions.explanation: Dead Sea water is very dense. Dense water gives more upthrust, so floating is easier.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is the law of floatation?
options: A floating body has zero mass
A floating body displaces no liquid
A floating body displaces fluid equal to its own weight
A floating body must be denser than liquid
questions.explanation: A floating body displaces fluid equal to its own weight. This is the law of floatation.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Why does a steel pin sink but a steel plate may float?
options: The plate can displace enough water due to its shape
questions.explanation: A steel plate can spread out and displace more water. So it may get enough upthrust to float.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Why may a boat sink if overloaded?
options: Its weight becomes greater than the maximum upthrust possible
questions.explanation: Overloading increases the boat's weight. If weight becomes more than upthrust, the boat sinks.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is a hydrometer used for?
questions.explanation: A hydrometer measures relative density of liquids. It works by floating.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is a lactometer used for?
options: Testing purity or density of milk
questions.explanation: A lactometer tests milk density or purity. It is a special type of hydrometer.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Why does a submarine change its position in water?
options: By changing the amount of water in its tanks and hence its average density
questions.explanation: A submarine changes water in its tanks. This changes its average density and position in water.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Why does a hot-air balloon rise?
options: Heated air inside becomes less dense than surrounding air
questions.explanation: Hot air is less dense than surrounding air. So the balloon gets enough upthrust to rise.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which factor affects upthrust on an object in a liquid?
questions.explanation: Upthrust depends on displaced liquid. More displaced volume gives more upthrust.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: How does liquid density affect upthrust?
options: Lower density always gives greater upthrust
Greater density gives greater upthrust for same displaced volume
questions.explanation: Denser liquid has more weight in the same volume. So it gives greater upthrust.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What happens to an egg in salty water compared with fresh water?
options: It floats more easily because salty water is denser
questions.explanation: Salt water is denser than fresh water. So the egg gets more upthrust and floats more easily.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: In a hydraulic lift, why can a small force lift a heavy load?
options: Pressure is transmitted equally and larger piston has larger area
questions.explanation: Pressure is transmitted equally in the liquid. A larger piston gives larger force.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which relation is correct for a hydraulic machine?
questions.explanation: In hydraulic machines, pressure is equal. So F1/A1 = F2/A2.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Why must hydraulic liquids be nearly incompressible?
options: To transmit pressure without large volume change
To become solid at room temperature
questions.explanation: Hydraulic liquid must carry pressure well. If it compresses too much, the machine will not work properly.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: If an object floats just below water and salt is added, what will happen?
options: It sinks more because upthrust decreases
It rises because water density and upthrust increase
questions.explanation: Adding salt makes water denser. Denser water gives more upthrust, so the object rises.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: When does an object sink in a liquid?
options: When its weight is greater than the upthrust
When upthrust is greater than weight
When it displaces no space but has no weight
questions.explanation: An object sinks when its weight is greater than upthrust. Downward force wins.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: When does an object float at rest?
options: When its mass changes every second
When its weight and upthrust are balanced
questions.explanation: An object floats at rest when weight and upthrust are equal. The forces are balanced.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which option correctly links instrument and principle?
questions.explanation: A lactometer works by floating and upthrust. So it follows Archimedes' principle.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: A person applies force on the larger piston to lift a load on the smaller piston. What advice matches the chapter?
options: Use no liquid in the machine
Apply force on the smaller piston and keep the load on the larger piston
Make both pistons open to air only
Use a smaller output area for heavy load
questions.explanation: Force should be applied on the smaller piston. The larger piston then gives a bigger output force.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: A ship floats but a small iron nail sinks. Which conclusion is best?
options: Only material decides in every case
Shape and volume of displaced water decide floatation with weight
questions.explanation: A ship displaces a large volume of water, so it gets enough upthrust. A small iron nail cannot displace enough water.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Why does pressure at the bottom of a liquid container exceed pressure near the surface?
options: Because liquid depth is greater at the bottom
Because gravity is absent at surface
Because bottom liquid has no mass
Because air pressure acts only sideways
questions.explanation: Liquid pressure increases with depth. So pressure is greater at the bottom.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: If the output piston area is five times input area in a hydraulic machine, what happens to output force ideally?
options: It becomes five times the input force
questions.explanation: In a hydraulic machine, force is proportional to area. Five times area gives five times output force.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which pair best compares pressure and upthrust?
options: Pressure acts only upward; upthrust acts per unit area
Pressure is force per unit area; upthrust is upward force by fluid
questions.explanation: Pressure is force per unit area. Upthrust is upward force given by a fluid.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Why can a hydrogen balloon rise in air though it has weight?
options: The weight of displaced air is greater than the balloon's weight
Gravity does not act on gases
questions.explanation: The displaced air has weight and gives upthrust. If this upthrust is more than balloon weight, it rises.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: A floating object is pushed deeper into water and then released. Why does it come back up?
options: Upthrust becomes greater than its weight until it returns to equilibrium
questions.explanation: Pushing the object deeper displaces more water. Extra upthrust pushes it back up.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which statement about Archimedes' principle is most accurate?
options: It applies only to objects in vacuum
It applies to objects wholly or partly immersed in fluid
It applies only to light rays
It applies only to hot solids
questions.explanation: Archimedes' principle applies in fluids. It works for objects partly or fully immersed.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Why is a lactometer reading low if milk is diluted?
options: Diluted milk has lower density, so the stem sinks more
questions.explanation: Diluted milk has lower density. So the lactometer sinks more and reading becomes low.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which condition makes a body remain suspended inside a liquid?
options: Its weight is greater than upthrust
questions.explanation: A body remains suspended when upward upthrust equals downward weight. The forces are balanced.
